hooks.text: A city-killer asteroid missed Earth by just six hours.
How did a giant asteroid fly past Earth completely unseen?
Six hours is all that saved Earth from a 300-meter asteroid.

title: The asteroid that missed Earth by six hours
description: A 300-meter asteroid crossed Earth's orbital path in 1989 just six hours after our planet left, and nobody saw it coming.

beats.text: A city-killer asteroid missed Earth by just six hours.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a near-Earth asteroid passing close to our planet, 2019

beats.text: Most people naturally assume our global detection networks would spot such a terrifying space hazard approaching days in advance.
beats.visual: Astronomical survey star field at Palomar Observatory, 1989

beats.text: On March 22, 1989, the 300-meter space rock named 4581 Asclepius crossed our orbital path completely unseen.
beats.visual: Diagram of Earth crossing asteroid orbit, 1989

beats.text: Astronomers Henry Holt and Norman Thomas only discovered the asteroid nine days after it had already swept past.
beats.visual: Samuel Oschin telescope at Palomar Observatory, California, 1989

beats.text: The massive object swept past us at a distance of roughly 684,000 kilometers.
beats.visual: Earth and Moon scale distance diagram, 1989
queries: orbit of the Moon around Earth diagram

beats.text: Geophysicists estimated a direct impact would have unleashed a devastating 600-megaton atomic blast.
beats.visual: NASA asteroid impact crater simulation illustration, 2019

beats.text: This terrifying blind spot drove the creation of modern planetary defense programs to ensure we catch every single city-killer asteroid.
